common_name: My Monet Sunset Weigela (Variegated Dwarf Weigela with Orange-Pink Flowers)

planting.note: Plant container specimens in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade in spring or fall; My Monet Sunset is a sport of My Monet with the same tiny variegated foliage but warmer orange-pink flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from the harshest afternoon sun where summers are hottest. My Monet Sunset is a sport of the popular dwarf variegated weigela My Monet, sharing the same tiny, tightly mounded habit and green leaves crisply edged in white, but bearing flowers in a warmer orange-pink tone rather than the straight pink of its parent. Its diminutive scale suits it to rock gardens, border edges, and container plantings where a full-size weigela would be far too large, and the variegated foliage provides season-long interest well beyond the brief spring bloom period. Prune only lightly if needed, and remove any solid-green reverted shoots as soon as they appear to keep the variegation stable.

common_name: Electric Love Weigela (Dark Foliage Hot Pink Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Electric Love pairs dark purple-black foliage with vivid hot pink flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade, where foliage color develops best with at least six hours of direct sun. Electric Love bears vivid, hot pink, trumpet-shaped flowers held against dark, near-black purple foliage, a striking high-contrast combination that provides interest well beyond the heavy late-spring bloom flush. Its compact size fits foundation plantings and mixed borders without the size management larger weigela can need. It is generally trouble-free, tolerating heat and average garden soil well, and needs only a light shaping prune right after flowering, since weigela sets next year's flower buds on the current season's wood soon after bloom ends.
